extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians serving as reviewers for Mathematical Reviews (American Mathematical Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, and submitting reviews (articles and books) to Mathematical Reviews, including what to include in content, acceptable lengths, timing, languages, and procedural options (transfer, index-only, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and primary content of a review
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should primarily help the reader decide whether or not to read the original paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review may range in length from a few lines to one or two double-spaced typewritten pages. In most cases it should state the main results, together with enough notation to make the statements comprehensible to someone already familiar with the field. The main ideas of the proof should be sketched when this is feasible. If the results are technical, requiring extensive notation or elaborate formulas, it is preferable to describe them with a few well-chosen and relatively nontechnical sentences. Helpful comments that evaluate the paper or connect it with related papers or approaches are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives to writing a full review
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted options instead of preparing a standard review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may recommend using the author's summary, with or without your signature, or a few sentences from the summary or text of the paper as the review (mark relevant passages and return paper or photocopy). You may recommend that the item be listed in the index without a published review (bibliographic data will remain searchable). You may recommend that the item not be reviewed or indexed. If you choose index-only or not-reviewed, return the item so editors can reconsider it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing references in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: When including references to related work, provide complete and verifiable bibliographic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full author name, year, journal name (or book title), title of the cited article, volume and paging. Include the MR number if possible. Because MR tries to verify each reference, include as much information as possible. Use no more than two references to related work unless absolutely necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative tone and evidence for criticisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may include positive or negative evaluation, but critical remarks must be substantiated and civil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative critical remarks should be objective, precise, documented and expressed in good taste. Vague criticism offends the author and fails to enlighten the reader. If the paper duplicates earlier work, cite specific references. If you think the paper is in error, describe the errors precisely. Be aware the author cannot reply in the pages of Mathematical Reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book review expectations and length
rubrics_metrics.description: How to review books and expository articles and recommended lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important new books deserve careful reviews. However, a good review does not need to be very long; less than one typed page is often sufficient. Try to limit reviews to a maximum of two or three pages. A detailed review is sometimes appropriate (e.g., expository surveys of interest) even if few new results are contained. Conversely, a book or article may need only a very brief description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time allowed for completing a review and related logistical expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maximum period allowed for completing a review is normally six weeks per item. This may not be enough depending on length and complexity. Promptness improves the timeliness of MR. If receiving too many items, notify MR. Reviewers outside North America should return reviews by airmail or e-mail; MR hopes institutions will cover postage, but will include return postage if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminder notices and when to return items
rubrics_metrics.description: How MR handles overdue reviews and what reviewers should do when they cannot meet timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have held a paper for about two months, a first reminder will be sent. If you cannot finish the reviews you have at the rate of one a month or faster, return those you are unable to review for transfer to another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return for transfer (inappropriate field/language/overload)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure if assigned an item outside your expertise, language skills, or capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return the paper promptly for transfer to another reviewer. No explanation is necessary when you return an article for transfer, but return both the article and the review sheet. Suggestions for alternative reviewers are appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to a colleague
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing a colleague to handle a paper and required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper could be better handled by a colleague, you may transfer it even if that person is not a regular reviewer; inform MR at once, giving the complete name and address of the colleague so the transfer can be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming inactive as a reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: How to pause receiving review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At your request, MR can make you 'inactive' and stop sending papers for review until a fixed date or until you indicate readiness to review again; send such requests to Reviewer Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred language and allowable exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are requested in English (since 1983 all reviews published in English). If you have difficulty writing in English, you may write reviews in French, German, Italian, Russian or Spanish and MR will translate them into English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript appearance and physical formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to prepare the hard-copy review manuscript that MR will use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hard copy, the review sheet you send is the manuscript used. Use only one side of the review sheet; continue on a separate sheet if necessary. If you lose the review sheet, send your review on plain paper and state the author, title, 7-digit control number stamped on the item and your name at the beginning. Ensure the manuscript is clearly legible with plenty of space between lines. Typewritten reviews preferred; neat handwriting acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission (TeX) instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for submitting reviews electronically using TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX is the typesetting language used in MR. Instructions for electronic submission of TeXed review manuscripts are given on the back of the table of contents page of recent issues. Electronic files can be requested by emailing mathrev@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit reviews in final, proofread form and note unusual notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please submit your reviews in final form (ready to be marked for typesetting if in hard copy). Always proofread your review before submitting it; this is especially important if someone else has typed the final copy. Explain briefly in the margin any unusual symbol or notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline on formulas to reduce printing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid excessive formula quoting; linearize simple expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help reduce printing costs by avoiding excessive or unnecessary quotation of complicated formulas. Linearize simple formulas using the rule that multiplication indicated by juxtaposition is carried out before division. (Example given: replace displayed fraction integral by (1/2pi i)int_G f(t)(t-z)^{-1}dt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting and font-marking conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How to mark fonts, special characters, and ambiguous symbols on the manuscript for copyediting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify ambiguities by marginal notes (e.g., 'one' (1) vs. 'ell' (l), 'zero' (0) vs. 'oh' (O), 'union' () vs. capital 'you' (U), 'wedge' () vs. 'vee' (V), etc.). Use the color code on the review sheet to indicate fonts. Greek letters should be written in by hand (or typewritten if available) and underlined in red pencil. Encircle script with blue pencil and underline Fraktur with green pencil. Boldface can be indicated by a wavy line in blue pencil. MR automatically italicizes mathematical symbols and does not use italics for emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject classification suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should suggest MSC (5-character) classifications for the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review sheet asks for suggestions for the 5-character classifications of the paper being reviewed. MR values these suggestions because reviewers generally have more expertise than the editors. The current classification scheme is published in the annual index issue and can be sent on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate reviews policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling reviews sent to multiple reviewing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MR has an understanding with Zentralblatt f9r Mathematik that allows MR to print the same review that you submitted to them. Please notify MR if your review has also been sent to Zentralblatt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating reviewing preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep MR informed of your research interests and language skills so appropriate items are sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MR bases sending articles on the reply card where you indicated reviewing interests and language skills. If you are being sent inappropriate articles or your interests change, inform MR of your current reviewing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and return of review items
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers may keep or must return papers/books sent for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers and books sent to you for review become your property once you have reviewed them. You should return a paper or book if you do not review it or if you recommend that it be listed only in the index. Also return an item (or a copy of the summary of an item) if you recommend using the summary as the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommending new reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: How to propose new reviewers and expected qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New reviewers are frequently enlisted on the recommendation of a current reviewer. Suggestions are welcome. A potential reviewer should ordinarily have already published reviewable work. Exceptions are made for strongly recommended recent Ph.D.'s, especially if they can offer needed combinations of expertise and language skills (e.g., Russian- and Chinese-reading reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and correspondence policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to direct administrative queries, subscription requests, or comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Reviewer Services for questions, complaints, or special requests. MR normally does not accept unsolicited requests to review specific papers. Subscription problems should be addressed to the American Mathematical Society customer service; editorial/contact email provided: mathrev@math.ams.org; webmaster@ams.org for comments.
